A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, principal problems, reductions, and theorem numbering. Their complete main texts, equations, five figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical reductions, proofs, and algorithmic bounds. Its figures illustrate mathematical constructions; neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. The added model definitions and discussion introduce no experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Section 6 broadens the ICNN model from ReLU networks to 2-maxout networks. The new Section 2 definition permits maxima of two affine maps and encoding skip connections. This is a limited architectural generalization; the reduction gadgets and LP/enumeration procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts training or evaluation on empirical tasks. The maxout addition changes theoretical model scope, not evaluated data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed method. Additional citations concern related work and do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental splits, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, training budgets, sample sizes, or testing procedures. The revised theoretical model definition does not establish an experimental protocol change.

E4.justification: The mathematical examples illustrating spike functions, penalties, homogenization, and zonotope containment are retained. No ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or error analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Section 7 retains the same theoretical high-probability approximation guarantees.

E6.justification: Neither PDF contains empirical result entries. The numerical examples and function values illustrated in Figures 1–5 remain unchanged; Figure 1 rearranges the same graph.

T1.justification: Section 2 adds formal maxout definitions and a CLIQUE-based definition of W[1]. The revised ICNN definition broadens Proposition 6.3's scope. Appendix B.4 corrects the positive-homogeneity attribution from g to h, while the principal hardness theorems, bounds, and proof arguments are retained.

C1.justification: The principal hardness and ETH optimality claims remain. The conclusion newly emphasizes hardness despite sparse, polynomially bounded weights and asserts that practical efficiency requires heuristics or techniques ensuring tractability.

C2.justification: The original worst-case limitations remain, but Section 8 adds discussion of structural restrictions, uncertainty about whether trained networks satisfy them, and verification-oriented training or special architectures. It also newly identifies W[1] membership of 2-layer ReLU positivity as an open question.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, experimental hyperparameters, hardware specifications, measured timings, or code/data access information are added or removed. The existing algorithmic constructions remain mathematical descriptions.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bhowmick et al. (2021), Splittgerber (2026), Ganian (2026), Baader et al. (2024), and Mao et al. (2024), covering Lipschitz computation, parameterized complexity, and convex relaxations. The introduction also contrasts the studied hardness with known FPT injectivity. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized introduction and conclusion revisions, adds the maxout explanation, and reorganizes Appendix B.3 to present node selection before edge verification. It corrects cross-references and wording, updates affiliation/publication text, and removes acknowledgments. The overall section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 rearranges the colored graph and adds explicit r/l class labels. All five figures remain; Figure 4 moves from before the surjectivity proof to after Section 5, and page layout reflows. No tables or new visual analyses appear.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity and auditability through clearer definitions, corrected cross-references and homogeneity attribution, and the reorganized reduction. Broader ICNN scope and updated related work/open questions add useful context. These gains are limited: central proofs remain, and the new assertion that heuristics are required in practice exceeds what worst-case hardness alone establishes.
